title: Top 3 Categories by Order Count
description:
Rank product categories by how many orders they appear in and return **only the top 3**.

**Table: orders** — `id`, `category`

Output columns: `category`, `order_count`. Order by `order_count` DESC, then `category`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, category VARCHAR); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,'Electronics'),(2,'Electronics'),(3,'Electronics'),(4,'Electronics'),(5,'Clothing'),(6,'Clothing'),(7,'Clothing'),(8,'Home'),(9,'Home'),(10,'Sports'),(11,'Books'),(12,'Electronics');
solution_sql: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY category ORDER BY order_count DESC, category LIMIT 3

test_cases.description: Electronics 5, Clothing 3, Home 2 — Sports and Books excluded

hints: GROUP BY category and COUNT(*) to get order volume.
ORDER BY the count descending and LIMIT 3.
explanation: Electronics appears 5 times, Clothing 3, Home 2, Sports 1, Books 1. LIMIT 3 after a descending sort keeps the three highest-volume categories. Tie-breaking by category name is unused here because the top three counts are unique.
